summary: Traditional education and upbringing often stunt our ability to **navigate uncertainty** because well-meaning parents and structured schooling shield children from the responsibility of **making independent choices**. Consequently, many academically brilliant adults struggle in business because they lack practice in **decisiveness and delegation**, which are essential skills developed only through real-world experience and trial. Effective leadership requires **embracing accountability** and making timely choices rather than stalling, since failing to act is typically more damaging than making a mistake. Furthermore, maintaining a high-performing company depends on **terminating underperformers**, as a leader's tolerance for mediocrity will ultimately drive away top talent and lower the overall standards of the organization.
